_provenance: schema-derived from López de Prado 2018 Ch. 7.4 and run_autotuner's 125-trading-day history window
_citation: López de Prado, M. (2018). Advances in Financial Machine Learning. Wiley. Ch. 7.4.
_description: Golden fixture for O6 60/20/20 train/validation/frozen-eval split on 125 trading days.

raw_fold_sizes._note: int(125 * 0.60)=75, int(125 * 0.20)=25, remainder=25. Integer truncation handled by assigning remainder to frozen-eval.

purge_embargo._note: Same PURGE_DAYS and EMBARGO_DAYS constants from O1. Applied at BOTH boundaries: train|validation and validation|frozen-eval.

usable_fold_sizes._note: After 20-day purge + 1-day embargo at each boundary: train loses last 21 days (75-21=54), validation loses first 21 and last 21 days (25-42=-17 => floor 0, realistically ~4 if boundaries don't fully overlap). These are approximate — exact count depends on calendar distribution. The key invariant is that usable validation and frozen-eval are small (~5 days).
usable_fold_sizes._fold_collapse_acknowledgment: At 125-day history with 60/20/20 split, the 20-day purge at each boundary leaves approximately 4-5 usable validation days and 4-5 usable frozen-eval days. This is an acknowledged tradeoff: the purge is methodologically correct (López de Prado 2018 Ch. 7), and the short eval windows are the cost of honest fold separation. Documented per O6 AC mandate.

_tolerance_note: Due to integer rounding on day counts, the actual ratio may deviate by up to 1 percentage point from the target. Tests assert within this tolerance.
